states.evidence_requirement: the citing court's own sentence, in its own voice, naming the authority AND the act performed on it. Not a heading, not a list entry, not a marker-terminated Case Law Cited line.
states.allowed_product_wording: may name the acting court and assert the act, e.g. 'Set aside in <citing case>.' Attribution to a court is permitted only here and in COURT_ORDER_DISPOSITIVE.
wording_forbidden: any 'set aside by X on <date>' provenance line where the citing span does not itself name the acting judgment -- 2 of the 5 spans do not, and the line must be omitted rather than filled from citing_judgment_id

states.evidence_requirement: the operative order -- set aside, quashed, reversed.
a court registry record of appellate outcome.
states.allowed_product_wording: NONE. MUST NOT appear in product copy, coverage claims, admin figures, or website/founder material as a source LawMind has.
states.currentness_propagation: MUST NOT -- zero available evidence. ecourts_observation holds 0 rows and the round forbids live eCourts traffic.
states.note: kept in the vocabulary so a future registry feed has somewhere to land. Naming an evidence class we cannot populate is how a capability gets claimed by accident.

states.evidence_requirement: a law report's editorial apparatus -- headnote, Case Law Cited entry, marker-terminated list line, column letters, page-and-line pins.
states.allowed_product_wording: MUST attribute to the reporter and MUST NOT attribute to a court. Permitted: 'A law report records this as overruled. We have not confirmed this against the deciding court.'
wording_forbidden: any phrasing whose grammatical subject is a court
states.currentness_propagation: MUST NOT write judgments.overruled_status. Render-time signal derived live from the edge, never a stored canonical status.
states.matter_workflow_note: MAY be shown on the authority inside a matter. MUST NOT disable add-to-matter -- a refusal is a claim, and this evidence cannot carry one. Today it already does not: OD-14's edge-derived policy allows every reporter-backed badge. The rule is written so a future change cannot reintroduce it.
states.briefing_note: MAY appear, qualified. MUST NOT be silently omitted. MUST NOT be stated as a fact about what a court held.
states.counterargument_note: MAY raise the point ('opposing counsel may say this has been overruled; a law report records it so'). MUST NOT assert it has been.
states.law_moved_note: visible, unmissable, explicitly sourced to the reporter, and visually distinguishable from FULL. Nothing is removed.
states.interim_product_direction: remains visible as a SAFETY SIGNAL, explicitly qualified, never presented as though the later court itself has been independently verified to have so held

states.evidence_requirement: the span is counsel's submission -- 'learned counsel placed reliance on X'.
states.allowed_product_wording: NONE. MUST NOT surface as treatment at all.
states.counterargument_note: MAY be read as evidence that an argument was made, never as evidence of what was decided. The one place this class has value.
states.note: classifier precedence is deliberately pessimistic -- a span carrying both counsel voice and court voice is classified COUNSEL_ARGUMENT, costing coverage rather than risking a false promotion.

states.evidence_requirement: the verb is right and its MOOD is wrong -- 'is sought to be overruled', 'proposed to be delivered', a dissent describing what the majority is about to do.
states.allowed_product_wording: NONE, pending re-adjudication. MUST NOT surface in any advocate-facing surface.

instance.speaker: THAKKAR, J., dissenting
instance.drives: a live set_aside, as sole driving edge

states.note: a quarantine, not a verdict: the claim has been read and found unsafe in a way the vocabulary could not previously express. The badge it drives is probably right and is right by luck. Re-adjudication needs the MAJORITY judgment read as primary evidence (NEW2-1b).

states.evidence_requirement: a reader or writer examined the span and could not attribute a speaker.
states.hard_rule: UNKNOWN MUST NOT be promoted to any other class, in any direction, by any process -- not to reporter, not to court, and above all not to a clean state. UNKNOWN -> anything is the same failure as SCREENED_NO_DAMAGE_FOUND -> 'clean'.

states.evidence_requirement: NONE -- nothing has looked at this edge.
states.hard_rule: NULL and UNKNOWN are different and MUST NEVER be merged. NULL is NOT LOOKED AT; UNKNOWN is LOOKED AT AND UNDECIDABLE. They want opposite work -- NULL wants a classifier run, UNKNOWN wants a human. A NULL edge is not evidence of safety.

corrections.withdrawn_claim: 72 of 76 add-to-matter refusals rest on a law reporter headnote alone
corrections.what_was_wrong: counted judgments.overruled_status='set_aside' (76, correctly) and called it add-to-matter refusals, from the remembered CLAUDE.md rule rather than from precedentialEffectFromEdges + precedentialPolicy which actually compute it
corrections.why: OD-14 resolved 21 Aug: the refusal derives from the EDGE, not the stored column. An 'overruled' edge maps to effect 'overruled' whose policy is 'allow'. Only a bare set_aside with no usable edge refuses.
corrections.effect_on_recommendation: strengthens it -- the priced cost of court-only-canonical was 72 refusals and that cost does not exist. The remaining real cost is DISPLAY only: 99 of 104 badges move from asserted to attributed.
